newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraq seen aiming at new attack on Kuwait, Kurds say.
newsitem.headline: Iraq seen aiming at new attack on Kuwait, Kurds say.

text.p: A Kurdish Iraqi opposition leader said in remarks published on Tuesday that Baghdad was trying to rebuild its power to repeat its 1990 attack on Kuwait.

"I believe the Iraqi government is seeking to rebuild its forces, and it will seize any opportunity to attack Kuwait again," Jalal Talabani, secretary general of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), told Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.
"There is no change in the mentality that dominated the Iraqi rule," he added. "This mentality...is a danger to the people of Iraq and the neighbours of Iraq."
Iraq invaded oil-rich Kuwait in 1990 and annexed it as its 19th province for seven months until a U.S.-led coalition ejected Baghdad's troops in the 1991 Gulf War.

Iraq's military strength was weakened in the six-week offensive. But in 1994 Iraq massed tens of thousands of troops near its border with the Gulf state provoking Kuwait's Western allies to swiftly dispatch troops to the region to prevent a possible repetition of the 1990 blitz.
Kuwait has about one tenth of the world's crude reserves.
Talabani, who did not elaborate on Iraq's efforts to rebuild its power, predicted an imminent change of rule in Iraq if Kurdish and other Iraqi opposition factions coordinated efforts.
Diplomats say the Iraqi opposition is deeply fragmented, which makes their goal of toppling Iraqi President Saddam Hussein hard to achieve.
Talabani's PUK often clashes with other Kurdish groups. One rival group sided with Iraq last year to overwhelm PUK forces.

The Kurdish leader also complained of a lack of international support for the Iraqi opposition. "As a matter of fact I do not find comprehensive support for the Iraqi opposition, be it regionally or internationally."

"We have expected Kuwait to be a firm...supporter of the Iraqi oppostion," Talabani said. "(But) we did not receive financial, military or political support, despite our repeated attempts with the State of Kuwait."
